lawyer:
Probir Neogi, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
SM Maniruzzaman, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 2. Muhammad Ali, Advocate—For Respondent No. 4.
parties:
MM Badshah Shirazi ----- Petitioner
Vs
Judge Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka & others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Moinul Islam Chowdhury J : Supplementary Affidavit filed on behalf of the Writ Petitioner be formed part of the original Writ Petition.

2. At the instance of the Writ Petitioner, MM Badshah Shirazi, Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate, Dhaka, this Rule was issued calling upon the respondent Nos. 2 to 14 to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 150 dated 5-2-2006 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1996 arising out of the Title Execution Case No. 151 of 1991 rejecting the application under Order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure (Annexure-B) shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. The relevant facts for disposal of this Rule are that the Petitioner is the superintendent of Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate and he has been directed by the Waqf Administrator, Bangladesh and authorised by the Hossaini Dalan Management Committee to initiate and conduct legal proceedings and to take appropriate steps in respect of the property in question.

4. It is stated that historically this case property is an important religion Waqf Estate. The property appertaining to CS plots No. 104 and 105 of CS Khatian No. 11148, Touzi No. 3241-B1, CS Sheet No. 19 of Ward No. 16 under Police Station Kotwali, Dhaka including the land, buildings, tanks, gates, compounds, walls together with many tombs and structures thereon belong to Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate, which is a public Waqf having EC No. 11737 (Dhaka). The Hossaini Dalan is an Imambara, which was created and permanently dedicated in the name of God about 350 years ago by Mir Murad, a pious and wealthy Admiral of the Mughal Navy in Bengal, for the public purposes of pious, religious and charitable nature to commemorate the tragic and noble martyrdom of Hazrat Imam Hussain (AS) at Karbala, and has been ever since used, treated and possessed, as such, by the Muslims in general and the members of the Shia community in particular from generation to gene-ration. The Waqf Estate successfully received the patronage and superintendence of the Mughal Emperors, Nawabs and Subedars of Bengal, the East India Company, the Government of India, the Government of Pakistan and finally, the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

5. It is also stated that in or about 1844 AD a committee of four Muslim gentlemen including Nawab Khawaja Alimullah, the founder of the Nawab family of Dhaka, was appointed by the Government of India to superintendent the affairs of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. In 1864 another committee of three Muslim gentlemen including Nawab Khawaja Sir Abdul Gani was appointed to look after the affairs of the Imambara. In 1891 the Government appointed Nawab Khawaja Sir Ahsanullah to supervise the affairs of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. After the death of Nawab Khawaja Sir Ahsanullah in 1901, his son Nawab Khawaja Sir Salimullah was appointed to supervise the affairs of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. After his death in 1915, his son Nawab Khawaja Habibullah Bahadur was entrusted with the same task. He being in sole charge of the Waqf Estate since 1916 was also appointed Mutawalli of the same after the Bengal Waqf Act, 1934 came into force. Subsequently, the said Waqf Estate was registered as a public Waqf in the office of the Waqf Commissioner, East Pakistan under EC No. 11737. Late Nawab Khawaja Habibullah Bahadur functioned as Mutawalli of the Estate till he breathed his last on 21-11-1958. Thereafter, the Government of East Pakistan formed a Committee for the management and supervision of the Hossaini Dalan Imambara. Justice Ispahani was the Chairman and Nawab Khawaja Hassan Askari and some other leading persons from the Shia Community were the members of the said Committee. After independence of Bangladesh a new Managing Committee was formed with renowned legal expert Mr Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed in the chair. On 30-12-1986 another Managing Committee was formed with Mirza Mehdi Ispahani, in the chair. After his death on 20-1-2004 Mirza Behrooz Ispahani has been appointed the Chairman of the Managing Committee by the Government. Under the guidance and control of the Managing Committee there is a Superintendent to perform his duties of maintenance and management of the Waqf Estate. The petitioner is the present Superintendent of Hossaini Dalan Imambara.

6. It is stated that total area of land belonged to Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate appertaining to CS Plots No.104 and 105 is 2.8140 acres. Out of the said quantum of land 1. 9300 acres of land appertaining to CS plot No. 105 is under Khas possession of the Waqf Estate which is known as Hossaini Dalan Building Compound. The other part of the Waqf property comprising an area of 0.8840 acre of land is locally known as 'Gas Garden' and appertaining to CS Plot No. 104 and bounded on all sides by pucca walls and on the south by homestead of Md Yakub, on the north by Hossaini Dalan Road, on the east by pucca compound of Hossaini Dalan and on the west by Hossaini Dalan Road and is hereinafter referred to as "the case property." The case property was leased out to one Pearoo Mia Sardar, predecessor in interest of the present respondent Nos. 3 to 14 for a period of fifty (50) years by a registered lease deed dated 21-12-1956 by the then Mutawalli, Nawab Khawaja Habibullah which was executed with the sanction of the then Waqf Commissioner. It was stipulated in the lease deed that after expiry of the lease period in December, 2007 the lessee would hand over vacant possession of the case property to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate. The lessee had been paying rent to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate through the Mutawalli but subsequently, he became a defaulter in payment of rent. After the death of the original lessee, Pearoo Mia Sardar, his heirs who are the respondent Nos. 3 to 14 took loan from respondent No. 2, the bank and mortgaged the case property to the said bank in collusion with the bank employees concealing the fact that the case property belongs to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate. The borrowers having defaulted in payment of loan, the bank instituted Title Suit No. 244 of 1979 for recovery of outstanding loan amount against them. The Suit was decreed on compromise on 23-9-1984. But the defendant judgment-debtors having not paid the amount due to the bank in breach of the terms of the compromise, the decree holder bank put the decree on execution by filing the Title Execution Case No. 151 of 1991. The petitioner was totally ignorant of these facts till 16-1-1996 on which date he was taken by surprise to see an auction notice in the "Daily Inquilab" wherefrom he came to know that the case property was going to be sold in auction through the said Execution Case. The petitioner immediately brought it to the notice of the Managing Committee of the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate and the Managing Committee asked him to take legal steps in this respect. Accordingly, the petitioner engaged a learned Advocate, gathered information through him from the Court and obtained certified copies and came to know above facts.

7. It is stated that the petitioner, thereafter, filed an application under Order XXI, Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the Executing Court stating therein, inter alia, that the property described in schedule No. 1 to the Execution petition is a Waqf property which was leased out to one Pearoo Sardar by a registered lease deed dated 21-12-1956 for 50 years at a yearly rental of Taka 250 only. It has been provided in clause (g) of the lease deed that the lessee will surrender possession of the case property to the lessor on expiry of the lease period. The bank has illegally filed the mortgage Suit without impleading the Administrator of Waqf or the petitioner as a defendant and no notice under Section 81 of the Waqf Ordinance was issued before institution of the Suit nor any notice in the Execution Case given to the Administrator of Waqf in respect of sale of the Waqf property. The defendant judgment-debtors have no right to mortgage the case property to the plaintiff bank, the present respondent No. 2, to secure the loan availed by them. The case property is liable to be excluded from the execution proceeding. The said application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1996, thereafter, the decree holder Bank (respondent No. 2) and the judgment-debtors proforma opposite parties Nos. 3 to 8 (Respondents Nos. 4 to 9) contested the said Miscellaneous Case by filing two separate written objections. The case of the decree holder in its written objection, in short, was that the mortgagors became owners of the case property under the Government after wholesale acquisition of rent receiving interest, the petitioner has no right, title and interest in the case land and, as such, the Miscellaneous Case is liable to be rejected. The case of the judgment-debtors in their written objection was identical with that of the decree holder.

8. It is also stated that the petitioner examined himself as PW 1 and the decree-holder bank and judgment-debtors (the Respondents Nos. 4 to 9) examined one witness each in the Miscellaneous Case. The petitioner as PW1 produced before the executing Court the certified copies of CS Khatian (Exhibit 1), registered deed of lease dated 21-12-1956 (Exhibit 2), enrolment certificate date 15-1-1949 (Exhibit 3), photo-copy of SA Khatian (Exhibit 4), certified copy of RS Khatian (Exhibit 5), Mahanagar Parcha (Exhibit 6), and order on objection given in settlement office (Exhibit 7).

9. It is stated that the Artha Rin Adalat by the impugned order No. 150 dated 5-2-2006 dismissed the Miscellaneous case on total misconception of law and without properly appreciating the materials on record, and also on misreading of evidence, hence challenged this order by this writ petition and obtained this Rule.

10. Mr Probir Neogi, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that having regard to the provisions of Rules 58 to 62 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure and having regard to the consistent documentary and oral evidence produced by the petitioner establishes that the case property belongs to Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate therefore, the respondent No. 1 committed an error of law in rejecting the Miscellaneous Case. The learned Advocate further submits that having regard to the registered deed of lease dated 21-12-1956 under the provisions of the Transfer of Property Act (Annexure-C) and particularly, clause 1 (g), the case property being a lease hold property, any charge created or transfer made by the lessee is subject to the terms of the lease and valid up to the period of lease and, as such, the respondent No.1 committed an error of law in rejecting the Miscellaneous Case.

11. The learned Advocate further submits that the respondent No. 2 on total misconception of the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and overlooking the special provisions as to the Waqf property in the said Act, has dismissed the Miscellaneous Case wrongly holding that with the wholesale acquisition of rent receiving interest, the judgment-debtor lessee became tenants under the Government in respect of the case property, and, as such, the impugned judgment is passed without any lawful authority, as such, it is liable to be declared illegal.

12. It is further submitted that in view of the conditions laid down in the terms of the lease agreement and the tenure of the lease agreement for 50 (fifty) years the learned Courts below was under obligation to consider the legal position but by failing to consider the legal position of this Case the Executing Adalat committed a patent illegality which is apparent in the face of the records and such illegality apparent in the face of the records is a valid ground for certiorari and, as such, illegality renders a decision has been passed without lawful jurisdiction, as such, the petitioner is entitled to file this Writ Petition under Article 102 of the Constitution instead of a statutory remedy available under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. In support of his Case the learned Advocate for the petitioner cited the Case of O'Reilly v. Mackman 1198213A11 ER 1124, 1129 which is a Case of the English jurisdiction.

13. He also cited a Case of our Jurisdiction, namely, Anwar Hossain vs Mainul Hosein as repotted in 58 DLR(AD) 229 and also another Case of Abdur Rashid vs Additional District Judge reported in 56 DLR 573. The learned Advocate for the petitioner particularly drown to paragraphs 49 of the decision of this Division reported in 56 DLR 573 which reads are as follows:—

"49. Besides, when a Tribunal is established by a statute for a particular purpose and empowered to exercise its jurisdiction in accordance with the procedure prescribed, such tribunal cannot override or circumvent such procedure and pass any order it likes. If it does so, it acts beyond its jurisdiction. When the Tribunal goes wrong in law it goes outside its jurisdiction conferred on it. The Tribunal has jurisdiction to decide "rightly" but not the jurisdiction to decide "wrong". When a Tribunal commits an error of law in deciding an issue raised by it, it acts beyond its jurisdiction and, such decision of the Tribunal can be quashed under writ jurisdiction."

14. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that an application under Order XXI, rule 58, of the CPC, though numbered as a Miscellaneous case, it is an application in execution proceedings and a part of the execution proceeding. So, an order passed on such an application is an interlocutory order, not a final order, and thus, no appeal/revision can be taken there from as per provisions of section 44(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. He further submits that it is true that an appeal lies from an order under rule 61 of Order XXI of the CPC disallowing a claim to property under attachment as per provision of Order XLIII, rule 1(i) (iii), but section 40 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which provides in the following terms:

“৪০। এই পরিচ্ছেদের অধীন আপীল ও রিভিশন কারযক্রমে, এই আইনের বিধানাবলীর সহিত অসঙ্গতিপূর্ণ না হওয়া সাপেক্ষে দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধি আইনের সংশ্লিষ্ট বিধানাবলী প্রযোজ্য হইবে।”

15. Since the provisions of Order XLIII, rule 1(i) (iii), CPC is inconsistent with section 42(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, the provision of the Ain will apply, therefore, the impugned Order is liable to be declared as passed without any lawful authority, as such, the Writ Petition is maintainable as per the above provision which reads as follows:

“৪২। রিভিশন দায়ের ও নিষ্পত্তি সম্পর্কিত বিধান।– (১) কোন আদালত, আপীলে প্রদত্ত রায় বা ডিক্রির বিরুদ্ধে কোন রিভিশনের দরখাস্ত গ্রহণ করিবে না, যদি না দরখাস্তকারী আপীল আদালত কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত বা বহালকৃত ডিক্রির টাকার ৭৫% এর সমপরিমান টাকা আপীল দায়েরকালে দাখিলকৃত ৫০% টাকা সমেত উক্ত পরিমান টাকার স্বীকৃতিস্বরুপে সংশ্লিষ্ট আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে অথবা বাদীর দাবী স্বীকার না করিলে জামানতরুপে ব্যাংক ড্রাফট, পে-অর্ডার বা নগদায়নযোগ্য অন্য কোন বিনিময়ে দলিল (Negotiable Instrument) আকারে ডিক্রি প্রদানকারী আদালতে জমা করিয়া উক্তরুপ জমার প্রমান দরখাস্তের আদালতে দাখিল করেন।

(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর বিধান সত্ত্বেও বাদী আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠান এই ধারার অধীনে রিভিশন দায়ের করিলে উহাকে উপরি-উল্লিখিত মতে কোন টাকা বা জামানত জমা বা দাখিল করিতে হইবে না।

(৩) উচ্চতর আদালত, রিভিশনের দরখাস্ত গৃহীত হইবার পরবর্তী ৬০ (ষাট) দিবসের মধ্যে রিভিশন নিষ্পত্তি করিতে ব্যর্থ হইলে আদালত লিখিতভাবে কারন উল্লেখ পূর্বক উক্ত সময়সীমা অনধিক আরো ৩০ (ত্রিশ) দিবস বর্ধিত করিতে পারিবে।

16. Further more, the petitioner by filing a Supplementary Affidavit and annex ring therein certain documents in relation to (1) the legal entitlement on behalf of the Hossaini Dalan Waqf estate, for example, documents of restraining the said Waqf estate by the Administrator of Waqfs of Bangladesh and (2) the relevant documents in support of the entitlement in favour of the Waqf. The Supplementary Affidavit further contains documents in relation to disputes regarding Mutation, Records of right, proceedings under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and also sections 30 and 31 of the Bengal tenancy Rule, 1955 settling the ownership thereof, as such, the suit property is a property of Waqf estate on which the Waqf estate has sole entitlement, therefore, the impugned Order passed rejecting an application under Order XXI, rule 58 is not sustainable under the provisions of law which infringed the fundamental right of the petitioner.

17. On the basis of the above submissions learned Advocate for the petitioner prayed to make the Rule Absolute.

18. The Rule has been opposed by the respondent No. 2, (Uttara Bank Ltd.), and also by respondents No. 4 by failing respective Affidavit in Oppositions, although the respondents No.4 to 7 filed Vokalatnama in their favour.

19. Mr SM Moniruzzaman, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.2, vehemently opposed the Rule contending, inter alia, that the Artha Rin Adalat examined the documents and considering the evidence produced before it rightly passed the impugned order No.150 dated 5-2-2006 dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No.7 of 1996.

20. The learned Advocate for the respondents No. 2 submits before us that the heirs of the original lessee executed a mortgage deed in favour of the Bank by mortgaging the case property as security of the loan as per terms and condition of the Lease Deed which has empowered them to mortgage the property in question, as such, the Bank duly sanctioned the loan in favour of the borrower (the successors of the lessee), by accepting the Suit Property as a mortgage property. The petitioner has no right to say that the property had been mortgaged by the lessee or by his successors illegally.

21. The learned Advocate for the respondents No.2 further submits that the petitioner filed the instant Writ Petition challenging the impugned Order dated 5-2-2006 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 3, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1996 arising out of Money Execution Case No. 151 of 1991 arising out of Title Suit No. 244 of 1979 without exhausting the appropriate forum of appeal as per provisions laid down in the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 or the Code of Civil Procedure and, as such, the writ petition is not maintainable and the Rule is liable to be discharged.

22. It is also submitted that the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat after examining the records and considering the facts and circumstances of the evidences of the case rejected the Miscellaneous Case rightly, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged.

23. The learned Advocate for the respondents No. 2 prayed to discharge the rule as not being maintainable under Article 102 of the Constitution.

24. Mr Muhammad Ali, the learned Advocate for the respondent No.4 filed an affidavit in opposition contending, inter alia, that the admitted position is that the late Khawaja Habibullah Bahadur leased out the Suit Properties to Pearoo Miah Sarder by registered Lease Deed dated 21-12-1956 with a yearly rent for the period of 50(fifty) years. It is also stated that the statements made in the Affidavit in opposition of paragraph No. 13 mentioning some clauses of the Lease Deed for surrender of the lease hold property in misleading one. The lease deed stipulates that:

(i) The lessor hereby agrees with the lessee as follows:—

"(ii) That the lease shall endure and subsist for a period of fifty years from the 1st day of January 1957 to 21st day of December 2007.

(iii) That the lease hold interest thus created shall be heritable by the heirs of the lessee and shall also be transferable in any manner whatsoever by him and his successors in interest or assigns by way of sale, mortgage, gift, lease etc.

(iv) That the lessee and his heirs and successors have full powers to construct Semi permanent structures on the leased out lands and let out the same to others as landlord thereof etc."

25. It is also contended by the respondent No.4 that the lease as created with the above terms and conditions is a lease in accordance with the law of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949, is a lease in perpetuity i.e. permanent lease, therefore, made the following statement:

"(a) In the meantime, the then Government of East Pakistan acquired all rent receiving interests and the late Pearoo Miah Sarder became tenant directly under the Government. SA Khatian No. 2140 of Mouza Lalbagh has been correctly prepared and finally published with plot Nos. 5273, 5274 and 5275 Jote No. 97 with rent. Rent paid regularly to the Government. The petitioner never raised any objection thereof. It is also contended that the RS Khatian No. 1002 has been prepared in the names of heirs of late Pearoo Miah Sarder with respective shares showing therein with a wrong note, and the respondent Nos. 4 to 7 was registered objection and preferred Appeal there from and the concerned authority corrected the said khatian."

26. It is further contended that the present petitioner filed a Miscellaneous Case without depositing the required money under the statutory provisions. The Bank, as the defendant, contested the case but the petitioner failed to prove its title and the learned Executing Court rejected the prayer of the petitioner by the impugned Order and the petitioner, preferred the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 274 of 2006 which was also dismissed.

27. It is also contended that an application to the property from the attachment, if allowed or rejected an appealable remedy lies and the petitioner filed an appeal to the higher Court but it was rejected for non prosecution, thereafter, this petitioner on his present capacity filed this writ petition which is not sustainable in law.

28. Mr Muhammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.4 further submits that the present Rule is not maintainable under Article 102 of the Constitution as there are some statutory remedies available under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. The learned Advocate cited a case of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) vs Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 3, Dhaka in support of his case as reported in 11 MLR (AD) 308 = 59 DLR (AD) 6 and wherein the Hon'ble Appellate Division provided that:

"18. The decision in the case of Gazi M Towfique vs Agrani Bank and others reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6 further strengthens the view that there being special provision for appeal in the Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990 no application under Article 102 lies against the judgment and order of the said Adalat. It has been thus settled long back that the writ petition is not proper course for challenging the judgment of Artha Rin Adalat in view of provision for filing appeal being provided in the statute."

29. The learned Advocate further cited a Case of Trade Multi-Alex vs Artha Rin Adalat in support of his case as reported in 62 DLR 533 wherein this Court referring to an unreported Judgment passed on 17-8-2010 in Writ Petition No. 5746 of 2005 (the Oriental Bank Ltd vs Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka ) in the following terms:

"Therefore, it transpires that section 41(1) of the Ain provides that if any party to a Mamla is aggrieved by an order or decree, he is to prefer an appeal against the said order or decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat within 30 days. Under section 44 of the Ain interlocutory orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat cannot be challenged in appellate and revisional jurisdiction and so, writ petitions are maintain-able against interlocutory orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. Therefore, it transpires that the orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat which are not interlocutory orders are appellate orders inasmuch as the words' "order or decree" it has used in sub-section (1) of section 41 of the Ain. On going through the entire provisions of section 41 of the Ain it does not appear that the word "order" is meant only for the orders passed under section 19(2) of the Ain. Therefore, the order rejecting of execution case being a final order of the Adalat, the petitioner is to file an appeal against said order and the writ petition is not maintainable."

30. He also referred an unreported Case of Orascom Telecom Bangladesh Limited vs National Board of Revenue in Writ Petition No. 3477 of 2010 wherein the judgment was passed by this Court. on 7-10-2010.

31. On the basis of the above submissions the learned Advocates appearing for the respondent Nos. 2 and 4 prayed to discharge the Rule.

32. After considering the facts and submissions of the parties and also considering the Writ Petition and annexure therein and the affidavit in oppositions filed by the respondents and annexure therein, it appears that the respondent No. 2 filed a suit being the Title Suit No. 244 of 1979 for recovery of loan amount of money which was decreed on compromise on 23-9-1984 in favour of the respondent No. 2, Uttara Bank Ltd. And on breach of the compromise, the Bank put the decree on execution by filing the Execution Case No. 151 of 1991 and on 16-1-96 an auction notice was published for selling the mortgaged property. It is admitted by both the parties that the said property was originally belonged to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate and the respondent No.4 to 7 are the heirs of Pearoo Miah Sarder who obtained a lease from the Waqf Estate by a Lease Deed dated 21-12-1956 executed by Nawab Khwaza Habibullah Bahadur as a Mutualli of the Dhaka Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate as a lessor. The said deed contains several terms and conditions to be fulfilled and satisfied by the lessor and by the lessee. The said Lease Deed dated 21-12-1956 contains the following important terms: "11) The lessor hereby agrees with the lessee as follows:—

i) That this lease shall endure and subsist for a period of fifty years from the 1st day of January 1957 upto the 21st day of December 2007 AD.

ii) That the lease-hold interest thus created, shall be heritable by the heirs of the lessee and shall also be transferable in any manner whatsoever by him and his successors-in-interest or assigns by way of sale, mortgage, gift, lease etc.

iii) That the lessee and his heirs and successors shall have full powers to construct semi-permanent structures on the leased lands and to let out the same to others as the landlord there of and to appropriate to himself all the rents and usufructs arising from the same but at the expiry of the term of the lease, the Lessee shall leave all such structures on this land and shall not be entitled to claim any price or compensation for those structures which will then be regarded and become the property of the Lessor.

iv) That the lessee shall have the right to plant, trees and to enjoy the fruits and also those trees when the same dry up naturally."

33. Regarding the aforementioned Lease Deed, the parties made a conflicting submissions. The petitioner claimed that it was simply a periodical lease clearly agreed to be expired after 50 years which created no right for assuming ownership, whereas, the respondents claimed that it created a perpetual right. We will consider these aspects and also consider the role of the Bank and Adalat on these matters.

34. Now, the most important question before us to settle and decide is as to whether the impugned order dated 5-2-2006 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat on an application under order XXI Rule 58 in the proceeding of the Artha Execution Case No. 151 of 1991 rejecting the application should be declared to be passed without lawful authority or not. In this regard, we have to examine the provisions as contain in order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil procedure which read as follows:

"Rule 58: Investigation of claims to, and objections to attachment of, attached property." (1) where any claim is preferred to, or any objection is made to the attachment of, any property attached in execution of a decree on the ground that such property is not liable to such attachment, the Court shall proceed to investigate the claim or objection with the like power as regards the examination of the claimant or objector, and in all other respects, as if he was a party to the suit:

Provided that no such investigation shall be made where the Court considers that the claim or objection was designedly or unnecessarily delayed."

<u>35. It appears from the above provisions of law that the CPC contains the said provisions as to investigation of claims and objections as to attachment of a property in a proceeding of execution of a decree. This provision is about investigation or enquiry to be made by the concerned Court under this Rule but it is not in relation to question of Title, therefore, if any order passed on an application under these provisions is not a final order rather it is an interlocutory order passed in relation to any property. It is a settled principle that under the provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, an interlocutory order is neither an appealable nor a revisable order; therefore, challenging a rejection order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat on an application under the said provisions is entertain able under the writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution.</u>

36. In reply to the question of maintainability of this writ petition as raised by the respondents the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the lease deed executed on 21-12-1956 was made under the provisions of the Transfer of Property Act (Act IV of 1882). In particular he referred to section 108 B(j) of the Transfer of Property Act which reads as follows:

"(j) the lessee may transfer absolutely or by way of mortgage or sublease the whole or any part of his interest in the property, and any transferee of such interest or part may again transfer it. The lessee shall not, by reason only of such transfer, cease to be subject to any of the liabilities attaching to the lease:

Nothing in this clause shall be deemed to authorize a tenant having an untransferable right of occupancy, the farmer of an estate in respect of which default has been made in paying revenue, or the lessee of an estate under the management of the Court of Wards, to assign his interest as such tenant, farmer or lessee:"

37. On the basis of the above provisions of law our view is that on expiry of the lease tenure in the year of 2007, the lessee's or his successors' interest or any interest accrued by a transferee or mortgagor or mortgagee has to be "subject to any of the liabilities attaching to the lease thereof' and would be subject to the terms and conditions of the lease. Accordingly, the lessee or heirs of lessee have to return the leased property to the lessor on expiry after 50 years as this is an important liability imposed by the lease deed upon them. Even if, the property was mortgaged to the respondent No.2 Bank by the present respondent No.4 to 7, they cannot ignore and/or deny the liability imposed by the lease deed either by the lessee himself or by the succeeded mortgagee Bank or any transferee of the interest and title of the lessor on the property.

38. On the basis of the above the learned Court below, particularly, the executing Court cannot overlook the said existing and prevailing legal position while passing the impugned Order dated 5-2-2006 by which the learned Artha Rin Adalat committed a patent illegality which is apparent on the face of the record.

<u>39. It is a settle principle of law that if a decision is illegally passed which is apparent on face of the record an illegal order, it is a valid ground for interference by this Court in the writ jurisdiction by way of certiorari. It is also a settle principle that if an order passed by the inferior Court illegally this Court has power to declare the decision as passed beyond a lawful jurisdiction.</u>

40. In this regard we can look into the decision passed in the English Jurisdiction in a case of O'Reilly vs Mackman as reported in All England Law Reports [1982]3All ER1124 wherein his Lordship LORD DIPLOCK categorically stated the above settle principle in the following terms:—

"A person seeking to establish that a decision of a public authority infringes rights which he is entitled to have protected under public law must as a general rule proceed by way of an application for judicial review under RSC Order 53, rule 1(1)a rather than by way of an ordinary action.

It was this provision that provided the occasion for the landmark decision of this House in Anisminic Ltd vs Foreign Compensation Commission [1969] All ER 208, [1969)2

c. AC I 47, and particularly the leading speech of Lord Reid, which has liberated English public law from the fetters that the Courts and statutory tribunals were concerned, by drawing esoteric distinctions between errors of law committed by such tribunals that went to their jurisdiction, and errors of law committed by them within their jurisdiction. The breakthrough that Anisminic made was the recognition by the majority of this House that

d. If a tribunal whose jurisdiction was limited by statute or subordinate legislation mistook the law applicable to the facts as it had found them, it must have asked itself the wrong question, i. e, one into which it was not empowered to inquire and so had no jurisdiction to determine. Its purported 'determination' not being a 'determination' within the meaning of the empowering legislation, was accordingly a nullity."

41. In relation to an alternative remedy provided by the statutory provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, it is true that there is an efficacious remedy available for the petitioner to challenge the impugned Order passed by the executing Court on an application under order XXI Rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure as it is appealable. However, in our jurisdiction there are a number of cases wherein this Court and the Hon'ble Appellate Division decided that where an illegality or error of law is apparent on the face of record of the Sub-ordinate Courts an alternative remedy is not a bar to invoke the writ jurisdiction under article 102 of the Constitution. Applying the aforesaid provisions settled by both in the English Jurisdiction and of our jurisdiction, in the instant case we find it clearly from the records and from the respective submissions made by both the parties that the clear factual position is that the suit property admittedly belong to the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate which was registered with the Waqf commissioner under the Waqf Act 1934 and thereafter the same has been registered with the Waqf Administrator of Bangladesh by the number of EC 11737 under the provisions of Waqf Ordinance of 1962. Thereafter, whoever came as the successors claiming their entitlement on the Waqf Property or mortgagee Bank lending money on misreading the vital terms and conditions of the Lease Deed dated 21-12-1956 shall be subject to return the property under the liabilities attached to the lease which is also subject to the provisions under the Transfer of Property Act and the Waqf Ordinance 1962.

42. From the aforesaid conditions of the lease and pursuant to section 108 (B)(j) of the Transfer of the Property Act, it is obvious that the lessor is entitled to get back the property after expiry of 50 years tenure of the lease period. In the event of the property be transferred or mortgaged or retransferred during the tenure of the lease deed, the transferee or the mortgagee or anybody can only get interest given for or during the valid period of lease, and such interest is subject to any liability attached to the lease deed. In view of the above, the Artha Rin Adalat and subsequently the Artha executing Adalat can only pass an order against the lessee the Judgment-debtor or successors thereof as their personal liability because the mortgaged property is subject to encumbrance of the lease deed dated 21-12-1956. Moreover, the decree holder bank shall become part of the terms and conditions of the Lease Deed. Accordingly, after expiry of the lease period of the lease deed, the present petitioner as a Mutawalli of the Hossaini Dalan Waqf Estate is entitled to get the suit property back at its present position without any liability for the loan granted in favour of successors of the lessee Judgment-debtors, however, the decree holder Bank certainly has remedies for realization of the decretal amount as per provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.

43. On the basis of the above finding the impugned Order passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 3, Dhaka has not been passed as per provisions of law as there is illegality apparent on the face of record, therefore, it was passed without any lawful authority.

44. During the hearing of the Rule the learned Advocates for the respondents submit that in the impugned Judgment there is a contention that the predecessor of the present respondent Nos. 3 to 7 got an interest from the Government under the provisions of section 10A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 known as "Rent Receiving interests held under Waqf. It is also submitted that such interest was obliged under Non Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1949.

45. Having considered the submission made by the learned Advocates for the respondent Nos. 2 and 4 and having perused the impugned Order in the record we are of the view that the said provisions of law is not applicable in the present case because section 20, sub-Section 2(b) of the said Act, 1950 provides a certain measurement of land for rent receiving interest. Section 20 (2) (b) of the Act, 1950 which reads as follows:

"(b) Lands in his khas possession of the following classes 2[other than derelict tea gardens], namely—

(i) Lands used for agricultural or horticultural purposes including tanks, Lands which are cultivable or which are capable of cultivation on reclamation, and

(iii) Vacant non agricultural lands: 3[Provided that the aggregate quantity of all lands of the classes referred to in clauses (a) and (b) in the whole of the province so retained in possession by a rent-receiver, a cultivating raiyat, a cultivating underraiyat or a non-agricultural tenant shall not exceed three hundred and seventy five standard bighas or an area determined by calculating at the rate of ten standard bighas for each member of his family, whichever is greater].

46. This provision has been eventually amended by reducing the quantity of the land by the Ordinance 1985, which is, the existing law, as such; we do not find any legal basis for acquisition of the suit land as found by the learned executing Court in its impugned Judgment.

47. Besides the above, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.4 informed us that he does not have any document to show as to the acquisition of land by the lessee from the Government, therefore, we are not deciding as to the legality of the loan granted by the respondent bank but we are here to decide whether the respondent Nos. 3-7 were entitled to mortgage the property beyond the tenure of the lease period and whether the Bank can sell the property after the expiry of the lease period or not in default to repay the loan amount. Our view is that the borrower borrowed and the lender leaned the money with full knowledge as to the terms and conditions of the lease deed, therefore, the matter of loan is simply a matter between the present respondent Nos.4 to 7 as successors of the lessee who are the judgment-debtors and the decree holder Bank but the petitioner as the lesser cannot be held liable for loan after expiry of the lease period.

48. In the above circumstances, the bank is at liberty to recover the loan money from the respondent Nos.4 to 7 as successors of the lessee by excluding the mortgaged property as a liability of the loan and bank also at liberty to recovery the decretal amount under the provisions of law of the Ain.

49. In view of the above discussions, we are of the view that assuming ownership by the lessee or his successors during subsistence of a lease deed or after expiry of the lease tenure i.e. 50 years is not permissible or legal under law. In the present case, on the basis of those facts and law as mentioned above, we consider that the impugned order has been passed which is error of law apparent on the face of the record.

50. Therefore, an impugned order which is not based on the provisions of law is passed without any lawful authority and beyond its jurisdiction which has infringed the fundamental right of the present petitioner and the impugned order is hereby declared to be passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

51. In the result, we find merit in the Rule.

52. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute.

53. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of Rule is hereby vacated. The impugned order No. 150 dated 5-2-2006 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Court No. 3, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1996 arising out of Title Execution Case No. 151 of 1991 is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The suit property attached under the Title Execution Case No. 141 of 1991 is hereby rejected.

The office is directed to communicate this Judgment at once.

End.
